messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING: multiple model-load failures observed in cluster-us-west-2 (gpu-pool-a). Error class: OOM / deserialization errors / nvrtc compile timeouts. Auto-escalating to #incidents and paging on-call.

mike.l: Confirming — started seeing repeated container restarts on nodes gpu-node-23, gpu-node-27 within the last 4m. Root logs show OOM during model init (alloc of 36GB). Also getting `deserialize: failed checksum` on a few artifacts.

ken-ops: I'm on it. Attaching quick log tail: 
```
[2026-03-15T02:47:11Z] model-service[pid=4123] ERROR model_load: allocation failed: cudaMalloc returned out of memory
[2026-03-15T02:47:12Z] model-service WARN kv_cache: invalid artifact checksum: expected=0x7f9b got=0x1b2c
[2026-03-15T02:47:13Z] compile: nvrtc timeout after 60s for kernel generation
[2026-03-15T02:47:14Z] container: exited with code 137
```

mike.l: Node metrics show sudden spike in resident GPU memory; multiple warmup jobs kicked simultaneously (batch size 64 warmup probe). Looks like a stampede.

sara-pd: Any customer impact yet? I see increased 503s on the hosted API for a small subset of customers. Not a full outage but latency and errors for r-saas customers in us-west-2.

eva.s: Observed automatic fallback to cpu-hosted model for some requests, which is causing long tail latencies. Customer-facing traffic ~0.8% of overall, but one high-SLA customer (r-saas) is getting rate-limited.

ken-ops: Immediate mitigation plan: 1) Pause warmup jobs on gpu-pool-a. 2) Cordon/drain nodes with repeat failures. 3) Route traffic to fallback pool in us-west-2-b (smaller models). 4) Clear compile cache and retry sequential warmup with lower batch.

mike.l: Commands I'm running: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-23 && kubectl drain gpu-node-23 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` 

ken-ops: Also running: `rdw infra scale-pool --region us-west-2 --pool gpu-pool-a --delta -3` to reduce concurrent warmups.

infra-bot: NOTE: Reserved capacity in us-west-2-b is at 70% — can take spillover but will increase latency slightly.

mike.l: After cordon/drain, restarting model-service on gpu-node-23 recovered one container but next warmup failed with nvrtc compile timeout. Suspect corrupted compile cache + older CUDA driver on that node.

eva.s: Hypothesis: two parallel issues — corrupted artifact for model:opt-llama-13b-v2 (deserialize checksum fail) and aggressive warmup config (batch 64, concurrency 6). Recommend disabling aggressive warmup for this model in pool config.

ken-ops: Agreed. Temporarily set warmup.concurrency=1 and warmup.batch=8 for model:opt-llama-13b-v2 on gpu-pool-a. Patch command: `rdw config set --pool gpu-pool-a --model opt-llama-13b-v2 warmup.concurrency=1 warmup.batch=8`

mike.l: Also replaced artifact on the affected nodes with a verified copy from artifact-store: `rdw artifacts fetch --id=sha256:abcd1234 --target /var/lib/models/opt-llama-13b-v2` then `systemctl restart model-service`.

oncall-bot: Incident marker created: INC-2026-0315-01. Severity: P2. Started at 2026-03-15T02:47:11Z.

sara-pd: Posting customer note: "We are investigating elevated errors and latency for some API requests in us-west-2. Our engineers are applying mitigations; some requests may be routed to fallback models temporarily. We'll provide updates every 30m."

eva.s: Quick test: warmup sequentially succeeded on a drained node after cache clear and reduced batch. No OOM. Releasing one node back to pool.

ken-ops: Rolling mitigation: 1) Pause warmups across the pool. 2) Clear compile cache on each node: `rm -rf /var/cache/rdw/compile/*` 3) Rehydrate artifact from store (verified checksum) 4) Apply warmup throttle at config level. 5) Monitor for 20m.

mike.l: I'm seeing one straggler process that crashed with driver mismatch: `cuda driver version 11.2, required >= 11.7` — added to incident notes, flagged node for full reprovision.

infra-bot: reprovision ticket created: TICKET-54321 (seq: reprovision gpu-node-27 -> driver 11.9). ETA 2h.

sara-pd: Are we doing an on-call handoff in 30m? My pager window ends in 35m. Recommend handoff to ken-ops if state is stable.

ken-ops: I'll take primary if the mitigations hold. Will keep the incident bridge open.

mike.l: Current customer impact: 0.6% of requests in us-west-2 are experiencing 5xxs; r-saas saw a spike to 1.8% for 10 minutes earlier. No confirmed data exfiltration or SLA breach yet, tracking closely.

eva.s: Added a temporary traffic rule: route requests for high-SLA customers to stable-pool-b with model:opt-llama-7b-quant (compatible API) to avoid failures. Ran: `rdw route-set --selector customer=r-saas --pool stable-pool-b`

oncall-bot: Reminder: add postmortem checklist entries and link snapshots: `rdw incidents attach --id INC-2026-0315-01 --files /logs/gpu-pool-a-warmup.tar.gz`

ken-ops: Handoff plan: I'll be primary for next 2h. Actions pending assigned: (1) reprovision gpu-node-27 (infra), (2) validate artifact integrity across pool (mike), (3) confirm warmup config change persisted (eva).

mike.l: Will run artifact integrity sweep: `rdw artifacts verify --pool gpu-pool-a --model opt-llama-13b-v2` and report results in 10m.

eva.s: Warmup config change confirmed persisted. Monitoring metrics dashboard — no new OOMs after throttle.

sara-pd: Thanks team. I'll post a short update to the customer channel and change incident severity to P3 if we stay stable for 30m.

ken-ops: Leaving the bridge open for now. If anything spikes, ping with :rotating_light:. Otherwise I'll start a timeline and RCA notes.

mike.l: Artifact sweep found 2 nodes with mismatched checksums (gpu-node-23, gpu-node-27) — both replaced and warmups restarted sequentially. No further checksum errors after replacements.

ken-ops: Closing notes: root causes likely a combination of corrupted artifacts (storage edge case), aggressive warmup concurrency causing memory stampede, and one-node driver mismatch that exacerbated compile timeouts. Follow-ups: (A) add artifact checksum gate in deployment pipeline, (B) add warmup throttling defaults when pool utilization > 60%, (C) schedule driver update for gpu fleet, (D) write postmortem.

sara-pd: :thumbsup: Assigning postmortem to mike.l and ken-ops. Will loop in product for customer comms.

oncall-bot: Incident INC-2026-0315-01 status: mitigated. Next update due 2026-03-15T03:17:11Z.

ken-ops: Handoff complete — I'm primary for the next 2h.

mike.l: Thanks — marking thread as the canonical incident log. Will attach artifacts and timeline to the ticket.
